name: Model/Actriz
label: True Panther
lede: Two Berklee kids, a singer they met in a Boston basement, one breakup, and a bassist who used to walk runways: the noise-dance band that got Pitchfork's 33rd spot for 2023 and a Coachella slot.

eras.title: Loud kids, a basement singer
eras.text: Drummer Ruben Radlauer and guitarist Jack Wetmore meet at Berklee in Boston and go looking for a voice. They find Cole Haden in a basement, and the band they build is angrier than he wants it to be.

years.src: Rolling Stone: Model/Actriz Interview · Crack Magazine: Cover Story · Wikipedia: Model/Actriz
years.h: A basement show, and a question afterward: want to join our band?
years.p: [[Jack Wetmore|e998aecd-25f4-4737-85e1-182a22e2e193]] and [[Ruben Radlauer|e6fd4e70-2475-4859-b97a-65a287ab3a54]] were shopping for a singer when they caught 19-year-old Cole Haden playing long, spoken-word pop songs. They asked him after the set.
years.xp:
Wetmore and Radlauer had known each other since childhood; their fathers played together in an 80s band. Crack Magazine reports the pair were looking for singers who fit loud music, and Haden's Laurie Anderson-style set of long, meandering pop songs with spoken word did not.

Radlauer told Crack they took a risk and walked up to ask. Wetmore told Rolling Stone that when Haden took the stage, their reaction was: "This is fucking sick." Sources differ on the year the band formed: Wikipedia says 2016, Rolling Stone dates the meeting to 2015.

years.src: Rolling Stone: Model/Actriz Interview · Crack Magazine: Cover Story
years.p: After local notoriety as "the cool, scary band" (Shapiro's phrase to Rolling Stone), Haden disbanded the group to say what he wanted to say.
years.xp: Haden told Rolling Stone the heavy-music frame left little room for what he wanted to express, and he needed time away. Crack Magazine describes the split as a product of difficulty writing material. Radlauer spent the gap joining, in his words, "a million different bands at once."

eras.title: Brooklyn, second try
eras.text: The band reforms around 2019 with a new bassist and a new city. Two years of shows, singles and a pandemic later, they record their first album.

years.src: Rolling Stone: Model/Actriz Interview · Crack Magazine: Cover Story · Wikipedia: Model/Actriz
years.h: Aaron Shapiro joins on bass and the band moves to New York
years.p: [[Aaron Shapiro|8625a5e5-8098-4f0b-9b33-2d9c30df64f4]], a former metalcore player who had also modeled, stayed for good; Radlauer says he "completed the band".
years.xp:
Shapiro was also a Berklee student. Crack Magazine describes him as an intense bassist with a metalcore background and a past as a runway model.

Wikipedia lists the four-piece, Haden, Wetmore, Shapiro and Radlauer, as the lineup from 2019 onward, with the group now based in Brooklyn. It also notes Alt Citizen named them one of its favorite live acts that year.

years.p: Two singles came out in 2020; the band was booked for SXSW until COVID-19 cancelled the festival.

years.src: Rolling Stone: Model/Actriz Interview · Wikipedia: Dogsbody (album) · Document Journal: Model/Actriz's Dogsbody
years.h: Dogsbody is recorded at Machines with Magnets
years.p: The debut was tracked in summer 2021 with [[Seth Manchester|e0e8139c-e211-4810-aa51-68806c74e234]] at his Pawtucket, Rhode Island studio.
years.xp:
Rolling Stone dates the recording to summer 2021, and Wikipedia lists Manchester as co-producer alongside the band. Rolling Stone also reports True Panther signed the band after seeing them play in Brooklyn.

The album went on to map the city in sound. Haden told Document Journal the record is "a portrait of New York", with memories he would meet again on walks through Brooklyn.

eras.title: Dogsbody, and everyone shows up
eras.text: The first album lands on True Panther, Pitchfork tags it Best New Music, and the crowds go from forty people to sold-out rooms.

years.p: The first single from Dogsbody went out on November 2, 2022, three months before the album.

q: Dogsbody is the perfect foil to Cole Haden's white-hot charisma.
years.src: Wikipedia: Dogsbody (album) · Document Journal: Model/Actriz's Dogsbody
years.h: Dogsbody: Pitchfork 8.2, Best New Music, No. 33 of the year
years.p: Pitchfork gave the debut an 8.2 and Best New Music, then ranked it No. 33 of 2023; Rolling Stone put it at No. 31.
years.xp:
Jayson Greene's Pitchfork review called the album "the perfect foil" to Haden's charisma. Singles "Crossing Guard" (January 17) and "Amaranth" (February 1) came before release on True Panther Sounds, per Wikipedia. The record was made with Seth Manchester and runs 37:52.

Haden described it to Document Journal as "my life, as a cabaret", and said he writes as "a gay person working in a genre that's not very outwardly gay" (quoted on Wikipedia). Wikipedia adds it won Best Heavy Record at the 2024 Libera Awards.

years.h: Forty people a night turns into sold-out rooms
years.p: Rolling Stone reports touring moved from 40-50 person crowds to sold-out venues after Dogsbody.

eras.title: Bigger rooms, bigger names
eras.text: A Barcelona invitation, a co-write for Miley Cyrus, a second album on Dirty Hit, and Coachella.

years.h: Primavera Sound invites them to Barcelona
years.p: The band was booked for Primavera Sound after Dogsbody, per Wikipedia.
The first single from Pirouette also became a TV moment, with the band playing it live on The Late Show.
[[Cole Haden|3c6ccacd-8c73-4fe4-88f8-1fef2b5bffe0]] is credited on the opener of Cyrus's ninth album, Something Beautiful.

years.src: Wikipedia: Pirouette (album) · Crack Magazine: Cover Story
years.p: Sophomore album, again with Manchester; Pitchfork gave it 7.1, Metacritic's critic average is 81.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists sessions at Machines with Magnets, The Cutting Room and Studio G. Singles were "Cinderella", "Doves" (March 25) and "Diva" (April 21). The Guardian gave it 4 of 5; Alexis Petridis praised its "thrilling contrasts" between cacophony and control.

Crack Magazine describes it as a shift toward dance-punk and electronics with the same confrontational live show.

years.p: Per Wikipedia, citing The Fader (March 23), the band dropped Swan Songs without warning.
The band played Coachella for the first time in April 2026, according to Wikipedia.
